book_paragraphs: We have reached the bottom line. Every piece of evidence across nine chapters—from KORU's 1H FY2026 Form N-CSRS filings to the November 20, 2026 market tape—points to one unambiguous conclusion for both new capital and your existing Robinhood shares.

First, let us put both sides of the aisle on the scale for new capital. A bull can rightly point out that Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are global AI memory champions, that unleveraged EWY still sits up +33.40% over the trailing twelve months, and that KORU's daily RSI of 29.77 near its $4.59 52-week low could spark a sharp short-covering pop at any moment. Those points are true, and they belong entirely to unleveraged Korean equities or a one-day dead-cat trade—not to deploying fresh investment capital into KORU.

The bear case wins on three independent pillars: Trend, Valuation math, and Cash-Flow carry. On Trend, KORU at $4.76 sits in deep Stage 4—down -80.64% below its 30-week SMA ($24.59) and -66.38% below its 50-day SMA ($14.16)—while EWY ($123.26) is also in Stage 4 and the S&P 500 is in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend. On Cash-Flow carry, Citibank's doubled SOFR+1.70% swap spread and 3.52%–3.55% money market yields leave KORU bleeding -8.43% to -8.65% annually. On Valuation math, probability-weighting our three 12-month scenarios—20% Bull at $7.07, 45% Base at $2.70, and 35% Bear at $1.28—yields a negative expected price of $3.08, or -35.3% below Friday's close. New capital is strictly REJECTED at TIER_0 across every horizon.

Second, let us address your existing position of 471.984153 KORU shares in Robinhood. Bought at a $5,457.78 cost basis ($11.56 per share), Friday's $4.76 close reduces the market value to $2,246.64—an unrealized loss of -$3,211.14, or -58.84%. That stake represents 2.99% of your $75,110.60 net worth, yet its 8.35 effective beta contributes nearly 25% of an S&P-equivalent position's volatility.

Most importantly, $4.76 decisively breached your prior $5.22 structural invalidation stop. Under our upward-only stop-ratchet rule, a breached stop removes all discretion: our holding action is EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 471.984153 shares. Because KORU just suffered a -25.04% single-day flush to a 29.77 RSI just 3.7% above its $4.59 52-week low, enter a tight limit order near the $4.76 quote—or use a market-on-open order if liquidity slips—across KORU's massive 93.41-million-share daily volume rather than risking a break toward Pivot S2 at $1.34.

Where should the freed $2,246.64 go? Because the US market is in an official Downtrend with only 38.8% of stocks above their 50-DMA and 10 distribution days in 25 sessions, cash is an active, high-value choice. We allocate 100% ($2,246.64) to CASH. Why not rotate half into Microsoft as we considered earlier in November? Because MSFT has since broken down to $484.52 in Stage 3 below its 50-day SMA ($519.84). And why not deploy immediately into Stage 2 Shortlist leaders ABBV ($286.20, $340.00 target, 1.85:1 R:R from $281.27 support and 1.47:1 at CMP) or LLY ($1,347.11, $1,660.00 target, 1.66:1 at CMP)? Because in a 10-distribution-day Downtrend, preserving $2,246.64 in cash protects capital until market breadth recovers or those leaders test support cleanly. Unleveraged EWY ($123.26) also stays at 0% in Stage 4.

Finally, our options desk confirms NO_OPTIONS_EDGE on KORU at $4.76. Walk away from KORU cleanly, bank the $2,246.64 in cash, cut 8.35-beta Stage 4 tail risk out of your portfolio, and wait patiently for the next confirmed Stage 2 bull cycle.

book_subsections.title: 9.1 Honoring the $5.22 Stop Breach Without Anchoring Bias
paragraphs: When a position is down -58.84% from a $5,457.78 cost basis to $2,246.64, human instinct whispers that selling at $4.76 locks in the loss. In reality, the market already marked your equity down to $2,246.64 on November 20. The only question today is whether $2,246.64 belongs inside an 8.35-beta Stage 4 ETF that just breached its $5.22 stop, or safely in cash.

Because 3x daily compounding works asymmetrically after big drawdowns, falling from $4.76 to $2.70—our Base Case 12-month expectation—requires a future +328% low-volatility rally just to revisit your $11.56 entry price. Cutting the position cleanly via EXIT_IMMEDIATELY ends that losing math today.

KORU traded 93.41 million shares on Friday, providing ample depth for a 471.984153-share exit. Place a tight limit order right around the opening quote near $4.76—or use a market-on-open order if premarket bids gap lower—so you exit cleanly before any break of $4.59 triggers panic selling toward $1.34.

book_subsections.title: 9.3 Why 100% Cash Beats Deploying Into a Downtrend
paragraphs: With the S&P 500 logging 10 distribution days in 25 sessions and only 38.8% breadth above the 50-DMA, retaining 100% ($2,246.64) in cash is an active risk-management decision. Look at why our Shortlist comparators wait on the bench at 0%: former leader MSFT ($484.52) broke into Stage 3 below its 50-day SMA, while Stage 2 defensive healthcare names ABBV ($286.20, 1.47:1 CMP R:R to $340.00 over $249.53 stop; 1.85:1 at $281.27 support) and LLY ($1,347.11, 1.66:1 CMP R:R to $1,660.00 over $1,158.67 stop) offer much cleaner setups once the Downtrend relents.
Likewise, unleveraged South Korea proxy EWY ($123.26) sits in Stage 4 at -29.32% below its $174.38 30-week SMA, earning 0% allocation until it builds a Stage 1 base and confirms Stage 2.

book_subsections.title: 9.4 Final Synthesis: Separating the Thesis from the Vehicle
paragraphs: Keep one permanent underwriting rule from this monograph: never house a cyclical semiconductor or Korean governance thesis inside a 3x daily swap fund with negative carry and 60% underlying volatility. Exit KORU cleanly at $4.76, hold the $2,246.64 proceeds in cash through the Downtrend, and revisit Korean equities only through 1x FLKR or EWY when Stage 2 returns.

book_subsections.title: 9.7 Why Capital Preservation in Cash Creates Optionality
paragraphs: Holding 100% cash with the $2,246.64 freed from KORU is not sitting idle; it is buying an option on future Stage 2 clarity. During a 10-distribution-day US Downtrend where only three of eleven S&P 500 sectors hold above their 50-day moving averages, cash is the only asset guaranteed not to suffer overnight gap risk.

Once market breadth improves and leaders like ABBV or LLY pull back cleanly onto verified support, that $2,246.64 cash reserve can re-enter the market on favorable reward-to-risk terms. Protecting capital today guarantees you still have dry powder when the next true Stage 2 cycle begins.
